newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Rains lift Tunisia crop hopes.
newsitem.headline: Rains lift Tunisia crop hopes.

text.p: Plentiful rains this month have made Tunisian farmers and agriculture officials optimistic about crop output for the new season.
"The important rainfalls this month and as to now were excellent and came at the right moment for wheat and the germination period," an agriculture ministry official told Reuters on Tuesday.
"They would also have excellent effects for the olive and citrus crops next season," he added.

January rains exceeded the annual average level in the northern cereals regions. "They not only benefit all crops but also are replishing the country's dams and groundwater tables considerably," an official said.
He put the planted to cereals at 1.8 million hectares.
The farmers' association said an excellent cereals crop was expected next season given adequate rains in March and April.
But they would not forecast a figure.
Tunisia had a record grain harvest of 2.87 million tonnes last year.

Drought cut the 1995 harvest to 0.62 million tonnes, and the 1994 harvest to 0.65 million after a 1993 harvest of 1.91 million tonnes. The previous harvest record was in 1990/91 with 2.56 million tonnes.
A recovery in olive oil output is seen at more than 250,000 tonnes this season, up from 60,000 tonnes in 1995/1996.
Domestic cereals consumption was estimated at 2.2 million tonnes in 1995.
